I hit the tool limit mid-build, so let me give you what I've established — the diagnosis is solid, and it's not what the script's output claimed.

What actually happened on virginia
Your run didn't hang. It did something worse and took 6m55s to do it:

postgres was crash-looping. podman ps shows Up 1 second (starting) for a container created 7 minutes earlier — the engine restarting it over and over. In the prior session it shows Exited (1).
web exited 1 and stayed dead. Exit code 1 is significant: it's the only clean exit-1 path in Program.cs — the configuration-error branch (Console.Error.WriteLine("Configuration error: …"); return 1). An unhandled exception from SchemaMigrationRunner would abort with 134, not 1. So the app printed a reason to its own stderr and nobody ever read it.
The script waited out the full 300s readiness deadline against an already-dead container, then printed the DEV INSTANCE — DETACHED banner with a public URL, held 20 more seconds probing that URL, warned it hadn't answered, and exited 0.
logs -f couldn't help — it only ever shows the tunnel's log, which is why you got 40 lines of cloudflared saying connection refused and zero lines about the actual failure.
The information you needed was sitting in podman logs myrestaurant_web_1 the whole time.

Two findings, both real
F-55 — F-53 was a wait with no deadline; this is a wait with a deadline and no evidence. A deadline stops a wait that cannot end; only a liveness check stops a wait that cannot succeed. And the failure path never printed a log. Also: up exited 0 over a dead instance, so time bash scripts/dev_instance.sh reported success.
F-56 — TUNNEL_TARGET defaults to http://localhost:8080, but compose.yaml publishes 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 — IPv4 only. run.sh has probed the literal http://127.0.0.1:8080 since M1; both tunnel helpers name the host. A rule applied to one example and never generalised (F-51's shape). BusyBox wget — the second entry in the script's own probe chain — does not fall back to a second address.
There's also a third, unfixable-by-restart case I found: down keeps the named volumes on purpose, and podman system prune -a doesn't touch volumes either — so a PostgreSQL data directory that cannot start (interrupted first initdb, hard reboot mid-write) survives every cycle you ran, including both prunes. There is currently no command in the tree that clears it.

What I have written so far
scripts/dev_instance.sh, rewritten (~930 lines, two parts drafted): both waits now bounded and watched — the database wait ends early on a crash loop, the readiness wait restarts web up to 3 times then gives up; settle skipped when readiness already failed; logs [web|postgres|tunnel] defaulting to web; new diagnose printing both log tails plus a reading key mapping each symptom to its cause; new reset (destroys volumes, confirmation required); describe_service reporting exit codes and restart counts instead of health: starting on a corpse; up exiting 1 when the app never answered. shellcheck 0.11.0 is installed here and your nine existing scripts baseline clean at --severity=style, so I can hold the new one to that.

Still to write: scripts/quick_tunnel.sh (loopback literal), .env.example, spec v1.13 (§14.3a, §16.4, Appendix A, changelog, header), OPERATIONS.md §10a, README.md, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md F-55/F-56, BUILD_PROGRESS.md Slice 28, a new DevInstanceLoopbackContractTests.cs (3 facts, 1059 → 1062), and _CHANGES.md. No files to delete.
